title: HTTP/SSE transport exposes all tools without authentication

evidence.note: main() supports --transport streamable-http and --sse; no authentication middleware, token, or API key is implemented. README line 445 explicitly states 'No HTTP authentication'
mcp.run(transport='streamable-http', host=args.host, port=args.port, path=path) and mcp.run(transport='sse', ...) have no auth wrapper

business_impact: Any process or user able to reach the TCP port can invoke tools that create/delete APEX apps, run arbitrary SQL, and create APEX users. In a multi-tenant or exposed scenario this is full database compromise. GDPR Art. 33 breach notification would be triggered.
root_cause: FastMCP server started without an authentication layer; design assumes localhost-only operation but does not enforce it.
remediation: Add bearer-token or mTLS authentication to HTTP/SSE transports, or proxy behind an authenticated reverse proxy. Reject requests without valid credentials before tool dispatch. Document the required auth model.
verification: Run apex-mcp --transport streamable-http; curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp without a token must return 401, and requests with a valid token must reach tool handlers.

title: apex_run_sql allows arbitrary SELECT/DML/DDL with trivial bypass

evidence.note: apex_run_sql accepts any sql string; is_select is determined only by sql.strip().upper().startswith('SELECT') or 'WITH'. All other statements are executed via db.plsql(), including DML/DDL and anonymous blocks
bind_params optional; no statement allowlist, no query planner restrictions, no row-level auth

business_impact: A compromised AI client or any HTTP caller can drop tables, truncate data, exfiltrate the entire database, or modify APEX internal tables. Disqualifying for any enterprise security questionnaire.
root_cause: No enforced separation between read-only schema introspection and privileged DDL/DML execution; a single tool performs all SQL.
remediation: Split into read-only and write tools. Use a strict allowlist for DDL. For reads, force bind variables and restrict dictionary views. Remove DML/DDL capability from the generic tool or gate it behind explicit opt-in with role checks.
verification: Attempt 'DROP TABLE user_tables CASCADE CONSTRAINTS' via apex_run_sql; it must be rejected. Attempt 'SELECT * FROM user_tables WHERE ROWNUM <= 1'; it must succeed.

title: Tool annotations may allow AI clients to auto-approve destructive operations

evidence.note: Annotations defined: _READ, _READ_OPEN, _SAFE, _WRITE, _DELETE. _DELETE sets destructiveHint=True, but annotation is the only control and is not enforced by the server
apex_delete_app, apex_undo_last, apex_delete_page, apex_delete_item, apex_generate_rest_endpoints registered with _DELETE or _WRITE annotations; no server-side confirmation or authorization check

business_impact: An AI client that auto-approves destructiveHint=False tools can delete applications, pages, or items based on a prompt without a human confirmation step.
root_cause: Server relies entirely on MCP client interpretation of annotations; no server-side confirmation, authorization, or audit of the human operator.
remediation: Add a server-side confirmation token for destructive operations. Log the acting human user (not just the tool name) and require an explicit 'confirm=true' flag for delete actions.
verification: Call apex_delete_app without confirmation; expect rejection. Call with confirm=true and valid audit token; expect execution.

title: Generated PL/SQL is built by string concatenation with only single-quote escaping

evidence.note: _esc() only doubles single quotes; no DBMS_ASSERT, no bind variables for identifiers or dynamic SQL
LOV SQL, IR SQL, and KPI PL/SQL built via f-string interpolation of table/column names and user-supplied SQL
Multiple EXECUTE IMMEDIATE statements generated from user-supplied sql strings interpolated into PL/SQL source

business_impact: Prompt injection or malicious tool arguments can inject PL/SQL into generated APEX applications, leading to data exfiltration or code execution in the APEX runtime context.
root_cause: No input sanitization beyond quote escaping; identifiers and SQL fragments are interpolated directly into generated PL/SQL.
remediation: Validate table/column names against a strict allowlist. Use bind variables for all values. For dynamic identifiers, use DBMS_ASSERT or a registry of known objects. Add a generated-code review step in dry-run mode.
verification: Supply table_name='EMPLOYEES; DROP TABLE EMPLOYEES' to apex_generate_crud; expect validation rejection. Verify generated PL/SQL contains no injected statements.

title: Single-user ImportSession singleton is unsafe for concurrent HTTP clients

evidence.note: ImportSession is a module-level singleton. session.app_id, session.pages, session.regions are shared global state
README line 444 documents: 'single-user server ... only one active import session exists at a time'

business_impact: Two concurrent HTTP clients can corrupt each other's app creation sessions, causing components to be created in the wrong application, data loss, or unauthorized cross-tenant modifications.
root_cause: Global singleton session instead of per-connection or per-token session state.
remediation: Scope ImportSession to the MCP connection/token. Store session state keyed by client identity and app_id, or document that HTTP mode requires one instance per user and enforce it.
verification: Run two simultaneous apex_create_app calls over HTTP; each must operate on its own app without cross-contamination.

title: apex_export_app writes APEX export to arbitrary filesystem path

evidence.note: output_path parameter is passed directly to open(output_path, 'w') with no path validation or sandbox
Writes full APEX application SQL export to the provided path

business_impact: An attacker can overwrite sensitive files (e.g., SSH keys, config files) or exfiltrate APEX exports to attacker-controlled paths on the server host.
root_cause: No output path allowlist or directory sandbox.
remediation: Restrict output_path to a configured export directory. Reject paths containing '..' or absolute paths outside the sandbox. Return the export as a string by default.
verification: Call apex_export_app with output_path='/etc/passwd'; expect rejection. Call with output_path='audit_exports/f100.sql'; expect success.

title: Database and wallet credentials stored in .mcp.json and environment variables

evidence.note: Example config stores ORACLE_DB_PASS, ORACLE_WALLET_PASSWORD, APEX_WORKSPACE_ID in plaintext JSON
All secrets read from os.getenv() at import time and held as module globals
Documentation instructs users to put plaintext credentials in .mcp.json

business_impact: Credentials are at high risk of being committed to git, captured in IDE/AI client logs, or read by any process with access to the environment. Loss of these credentials equals full APEX workspace compromise.
root_cause: No integration with a secrets manager; design relies on local env vars and config files.
remediation: Support reading credentials from a secrets manager (OpenBao, OS keyring) or short-lived IAM tokens. Mark .mcp.json in .gitignore and provide a .mcp.json.example only. Never require plaintext password in env.
verification: grep -R 'ORACLE_DB_PASS' .mcp.json returns empty. Server starts and connects using only a token/secret-reference, not a plaintext password.

title: Wallet password exposed to server process and weakly masked in requirement checks

evidence.note: apex_check_requirements masks env vars as 'val[:3] + ***' regardless of length; very short values leak nearly the entire secret
wallet_pass passed directly to oracledb.connect() kwargs

business_impact: Wallet password may appear in logs, error traces, or process listings; combined with DB user/pass it enables direct database connection.
root_cause: Secrets handled as plain strings through the stack; masking logic is insufficient.
remediation: Use a dedicated secrets manager or prompt for wallet password at startup. Redact all secrets in logs and health-check output.
verification: Run apex_check_requirements with a 6-character password; output must show '***' only. Verify no secret appears in server logs.

title: No architectural separation between AI client trust boundary and database privileges

evidence.note: All 86+ tools registered with identical trust model; no privilege tiers or role-based gating
Single ConnectionManager singleton used by all tools with the same Oracle user

business_impact: A low-privilege user (e.g., read-only reviewer) and an admin have the same tool capabilities through the MCP server. Cannot enforce least-privilege or separate duties.
root_cause: Server is single-role; all tools share one DB connection and one APEX workspace identity.
remediation: Introduce tool visibility/authorization based on caller identity. Support multiple Oracle connection profiles (read-only, developer, admin) and validate caller access before dispatch.
verification: A read-only MCP token can call apex_list_apps but receives 403 for apex_delete_app and apex_run_sql.

title: No documented GDPR lawful basis, retention, deletion or portability capability

evidence.note: No mention of GDPR, data retention, deletion, or portability
Audit log writes to ~/.apex_mcp/audit.jsonl with no retention policy or deletion mechanism

business_impact: EU customers cannot satisfy GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17 (erasure), or Art. 20 (portability). Blocks enterprise sales in EU and risks regulatory fine.
root_cause: Product built as dev tool without privacy-by-design documentation or controls.
remediation: Document lawful basis, retention periods, and deletion/portability procedures. Add config for APEX_MCP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS and a routine to purge old audit logs. Provide data-export API.
verification: Review privacy documentation; verify audit log older than retention period is automatically removed; verify export returns all data held for a named workspace.

title: Dependency versions float and no lockfile is present

evidence.note: dependencies = ['fastmcp>=3.0.0', 'oracledb>=2.0.0']
dev = ['pytest>=8.0']
Dependabot configured but no lockfile to pin exact transitive versions

business_impact: Builds are non-reproducible and a compromised upstream package can be pulled automatically. Supply-chain attack surface.
root_cause: Loose version constraints and absence of requirements-lock.txt or poetry.lock.
remediation: Generate and commit a lockfile (e.g., uv.lock, poetry.lock, or requirements-lock.txt). Pin CI to install from lockfile. Run pip-audit/renovate/dependabot with auto-merge disabled.
verification: CI installs dependencies using lockfile; pip-audit reports zero known high/critical vulnerabilities in locked versions.

title: No linting, formatting, type checking, or CI security gates

evidence.note: No [tool.ruff], [tool.black], [tool.mypy], or [tool.pytest] lint config
Only dependabot; no GitHub Actions workflow for test/lint/SAST

business_impact: Code quality and security issues are not caught before merge. Increases likelihood of injection bugs and inconsistent handling of secrets.
root_cause: No development pipeline automation beyond dependency alerts.
remediation: Add GitHub Actions workflow running ruff, mypy, bandit, pytest -m 'not integration', and pip-audit on every PR. Block merge on failure.
verification: Open a PR with an unsafe eval() pattern; CI fails on bandit. Open a type-error PR; CI fails on mypy.

title: Audit log is local-only with no integrity or off-box shipping

evidence.note: Default audit dir is ~/.apex_mcp/audit.jsonl
Best-effort append; OSError silently ignored

business_impact: Compromise of the server host allows deletion or modification of the audit trail. Forensic investigation and compliance audits cannot rely on it.
root_cause: Audit log stored on the same filesystem as the server process with no tamper protection.
remediation: Ship audit events to an append-only external system (syslog, OpenBao audit device, SIEM). Sign each entry or write to a tamper-evident store.
verification: Delete ~/.apex_mcp/audit.jsonl; verify events still appear in external SIEM and an alert fires.

title: No rate limiting on HTTP/SSE endpoints

evidence.note: No rate-limiting middleware or decorator around mcp.run() or tool dispatch

business_impact: Vulnerable to brute-force credential stuffing against any future auth layer, and to accidental or malicious resource exhaustion against Oracle.
root_cause: No throttling or concurrency controls implemented.
remediation: Add per-IP and per-token rate limits. Limit concurrent apex_run_sql executions and batch sizes.
verification: Send 1000 requests in 1 second; server returns 429 after configured threshold and Oracle connection count stays bounded.
